title: Linguistic Distance Segregates Latent Representations in Automatic Speech Recognition Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.30853v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While automatic speech recognition (ASR) models have achieved remarkable improvements in recent years, performance disparities persist across different speaker populations. One such disparity is for speakers whose first languages (L1) are from families distant from English. This paper investigates the relationship between first language background and English ASR performance. Through empirical analysis, we observe that the correlation between speakers' L1 distance and ASR error rates yields a systematic effect on English Speech, with its strength varying across datasets and models. This association is statistically significant in a follow-up analysis accounting for dataset-level variation in Tweedie mixed-effects models ($p<0.001$ across evaluated models). In addition, analysis of the latent space reveals a L1-based spatial segregation across deeper acoustic layers in the majority of evaluated architectures

translated_title: 语言距离导致自动语音识别系统中潜在表示的分离
translated_abstract: 尽管自动语音识别（ASR）模型近年来取得了显著进步，但在不同说话人群体的表现上仍存在性能差异。其中一种差异体现在母语（L1）属于与英语亲缘关系较远的语系的说话人身上。本文研究了母语背景与英语ASR性能之间的关系。通过实证分析，我们观察到说话人的母语距离与ASR错误率之间的相关性对英语语音产生了系统性影响，其强度因数据集和模型而异。在后续考虑数据集层面变异的Tweedie混合效应模型分析中，这种关联具有统计学显著性（在所有评估模型中p<0.001）。此外，对潜在空间的分析显示，在大多数被评估的架构中，较深的声学层存在基于母语的空间分离现象。
tldr: 本文发现说话人母语与英语之间的语言距离会系统性影响英语ASR的错误率，并在大多数模型的深层声学层中观察到基于母语的潜在表示空间分离现象。
en_tdlr: The linguistic distance between a speaker's first language and English systematically affects ASR error rates, with latent representations spatially segregated by L1 background in the deeper acoustic layers of most evaluated models.
